name: AgentCore — Memory Persistence & Actor Isolation Test

parameters.content:
## Memory persistence & actor isolation test

Go/no-go check for the two claims every memory-based template depends on.

### How it works
Three webhook paths hit ONE auto-provisioned harness with managed memory.

1. `POST /memory-test-store`: actor A stores a codename.
2. `POST /memory-test-recall` — actor A asks for it back, in a **separate execution**. Must return the codename.
3. `POST /memory-test-isolate`: actor B asks the same question on the **same Session ID**. Must NOT return the codename.

The verdict node asserts each result and returns `pass: true|false`, so you never have to eyeball the prose.

### Setup
1. Add an **Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API** credential (AWS keys, region, execution role ARN).
2. Select it on all three AgentCore nodes.
3. Activate the workflow, then run the three curl commands in the grey sticky **in order**.

Step 1 provisions the harness and takes ~30 seconds. Steps 2 and 3 return in a few seconds.

### Why it matters
Recall proves memory survives across executions. Isolation proves one actor's memory never reaches another. Both must pass before any template claims per-user memory.

## Run these in order

```
curl -X POST \
  <base>/memory-test-store

curl -X POST \
  <base>/memory-test-recall

curl -X POST \
  <base>/memory-test-isolate
```

Wait ~15s between calls. Copy `<base>` from a Webhook node's Production URL.

## 1. Store (actor A)
Writes the codename into managed memory under `actor-a`.

## 2. Recall (actor A, separate execution)
Same Actor ID, same Session ID, brand new execution. Expects the codename back.

## 3. Isolate (actor B, same session)
Only the Actor ID changes. A leak here means per-user memory is unsafe to ship.
